page: Vultr vx1-m-2c-16g is a memory-optimized virtual server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical AMD EPYC core with 2 threads, running at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is limited to a small 1 GB NVMe SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present on this instance.

Benchmark results show a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core execution is highly competitive, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression placing in the top 10% tier. However, due to the low physical core count, multi-core benchmarks like stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and software compilation with clang fall into the bottom 25% tier. Memory bandwidth for large blocks is average, while small-block cached read bandwidth is weak.

The primary tradeoff of this instance is its high memory capacity paired with minimal local storage and low multi-core compute capacity. It offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring a large memory footprint but minimal disk space and low parallel processing demands. Suitable workloads include single-threaded memory-intensive tasks, caching layers, lightweight text processing, and basic static web serving. It is poorly suited for database operations, heavy multi-threaded compilation, or large-scale LLM inference.
